detail.longDescription: I had a GitHub repository where I made my initial commits. I used Codex to remove potentially private details from the repository, and during this process the Git configuration/commit information was changed. It also created a new email identity using no-reply , which turned out to correspond to another GitHub user's account. I deleted the original repository and created a new one. I then pushed my existing local repository to the new repository using the new repository URL. Now, after making further changes and committing them locally, git push is rejected unless I use --force . I'm confused because the repository contains my own work, and I am the only person working on it. Why does Git think the remote and local histories are different, and why is a force push required? What is the correct way to fix this so I can continue pushing normally without losing any of my existing work?
